content: The unit ell, equivalent to 1.143 meters (for the international inch), was primarily used in the tailoring industry but is now considered obsolete. Its origin is attributed to the length of the arm measured from the shoulder (or elbow) to the wrist, although its precise length was never formally defined under English law. The ell was approximately 0.78 meters, or about 31 inches. Occasionally, the term ell was used interchangeably with cubit. An ell-wand or ellwand referred to a rod of one ell in length, which was employed for official measurements. King Edward I of England mandated that every town possess such a standard measuring rod. In Scotland, the Belt of Orion constellation was colloquially referred to as the King's Ellwand.
